deck_name: Mamluk Playing Cards — Mulūk wa-nuwwāb (the Direct Ancestor)

mamluk-overview.name: The Mamluk Pack — Kings & Deputies
mamluk-overview.Scene: A hand-painted card from the Mamluk playing card collection (now dispersed in the Topkapi Palace Museum and Benaki Museum). The card shown is from the cups suit, elaborately painted with arabesque scrollwork, intricate geometric borders, and an Arabic inscription panel at top identifying rank.

suit-cups.name: Suit of Cups (ṭūmān)
suit-cups.Scene: Pip and court cards of the cups suit (ṭūmān). Pip cards show the cup symbol — a rounded chalice form — repeated according to the card's numerical value within elegant geometric borders. Court cards bear Arabic titles in calligraphic panels: Malik (king), Nā'ib al-kabīr (upper deputy), Nā'ib al-thānī (lower deputy).

suit-coins.name: Suit of Coins (darāhim)
suit-coins.Scene: Pip and court cards of the coins suit (darāhim). The coin symbol — a round disc bearing a square or geometric inset — is repeated in the pip cards, arranged in balanced geometric grids. Court card panels bear Arabic calligraphic titles.

suit-swords.name: Suit of Swords (suyūf)
suit-swords.Scene: Pip and court cards of the swords suit (suyūf). Pip cards show curved scimitar-like sword forms arranged in interlocking patterns. The swords fan and cross each other in increasingly complex configurations at higher pip values.

suit-polo.name: Suit of Polo-sticks (jawkān)
suit-polo.Scene: Pip and court cards of the polo-sticks suit (jawkān). The polo mallet — a long staff with a curved head — is shown in various arrangements and multiples on pip cards. Polo was the premier sport of Mamluk military culture.

court-structure.name: The Court — Malik & two Nā'ib (aniconic)
court-structure.Scene: Three court ranks are distinguished on each Mamluk suit: the Malik (king) shown with a more elaborated border, the Nā'ib al-kabīr (upper viceroy/deputy), and the Nā'ib al-thānī (lower viceroy/deputy). Court cards are distinguished by the Arabic title panel and the elaborateness of their arabesque decoration, not by figurative images of persons.

cups-king.name: Malik al-ṭūmān — King of Cups
cups-king.Scene: A court card from the cups suit identified as Malik (king) by its Arabic title inscription. The card bears particularly elaborate arabesque decoration in the main field and a formal calligraphic title panel at the top.

cups-deputy.name: Nā'ib al-ṭūmān — Deputy of Cups
cups-deputy.Scene: A court card from the cups suit, rank Nā'ib (deputy/viceroy). Arabic calligraphic title panel at top; the arabesque decoration is rich but slightly less elaborate than the Malik card.

cups-pip.name: Pip card — Cups (representative)
cups-pip.Scene: A pip card from the cups suit showing the cup symbol — a rounded chalice form — repeated in a geometric arrangement within an arabesque border.

coins-king.name: Malik al-darāhim — King of Coins
coins-king.Scene: A court card from the coins suit, rank Malik (king). Identified by its Arabic title and the richest arabesque decoration in the suit. The coin symbol — a round disc with square inset — appears in the decoration.

coins-deputy.name: Nā'ib al-darāhim — Deputy of Coins
coins-deputy.Scene: A court card from the coins suit, rank Nā'ib. Arabesque field with a calligraphic title panel; slightly simpler ornamental scheme than the Malik.

coins-pip.name: Pip card — Coins (representative)
coins-pip.Scene: A pip card from the coins suit showing the round disc coin symbol repeated in balanced geometric arrangements within a fine arabesque border.

swords-king.name: Malik al-suyūf — King of Swords
swords-king.Scene: A court card from the swords suit, rank Malik. The Arabic calligraphic title panel identifies it; the arabesque decoration is the most elaborate of the suit. Curved sword forms may appear subtly within the ornamental field.

swords-deputy.name: Nā'ib al-suyūf — Deputy of Swords
swords-deputy.Scene: A court card from the swords suit, rank Nā'ib. Calligraphic title panel with rich but secondary arabesque decoration.

swords-pip.name: Pip card — Swords (representative)
swords-pip.Scene: A pip card from the swords suit showing curved scimitar forms arranged in interlocking or fanning patterns, contained within arabesque borders.

polo-king.name: Malik al-jawkān — King of Polo-sticks
polo-king.Scene: A court card from the polo-sticks suit, rank Malik. The Arabic title identifies it; arabesque decoration is at its richest for this suit. The polo mallet form may appear within the ornamental field.

polo-deputy.name: Nā'ib al-jawkān — Deputy of Polo-sticks
polo-deputy.Scene: A court card from the polo-sticks suit, rank Nā'ib. Calligraphic title panel; secondary level of arabesque decoration.

polo-pip.name: Pip card — Polo-sticks (representative)
polo-pip.Scene: A pip card from the polo-sticks suit showing the polo mallet (a long staff with curved head) repeated in geometric arrangements within arabesque borders.
